Deliberately leaves run history, usage ledger and connection metadata untouched. `CloudService.deployedStatus`/`refreshStatus()`/`removeWorkflow()` back the Cloud dialog's per-workflow deploy indicator + remove button (both providers, keyed on `activeDoc()?.workflowId` like `PortalPanel` already does - null when the doc was never saved to the library, since `exportActiveSpec()` mints a throwaway id in that case). No cross-workflow "list of published workflows" was built - the DO-per-workflow-id model already lets any caller derive per-workflow status from the local library without a new registry.
- 2026-08-07 - GOTCHA: adding a new HTTP method to a route in `workflow-agent.ts` is NOT enough - the browser's CORS preflight (OPTIONS) is answered by `corsHeaders()` in `index.ts` (`Access-Control-Allow-Methods`) BEFORE the request ever reaches the DO's `routeAgentRequest`. Shipping `DELETE /workflow` without adding `DELETE` there broke it with a browser-only CORS error (curl/tests never trip preflight, so `npm run check` and Miniflare tests missed it until a regression test was added dispatching a real `OPTIONS` request). `cloud/src/workflow-agent.ts`'s own `json()` helper has its own separate CORS header set (already had DELETE) - the two lists can drift; check BOTH when adding a method anywhere under `/agents/workflow-agent/`. Regression test: `deploy-validation.test.mjs` "OPTIONS preflight CORS headers".
- 2026-08-11 - Full cloud teardown on workflow delete / "Remove from cloud": `DELETE /workflow` only nulled the spec and left the DO, SQLite tables, portal slug, session DOs and cron all orphaned (a deleted workflow's portal kept serving visitors, burning credits). Added `DELETE /workflow/purge` (full teardown via `WorkflowAgent.purgeSelf(cascade)` RPC): cancel cron, `portalIndex.unpublish` + `deleteSessions`, wipe `run_journal`/`runs`/`run_events`/`usage_ledger`/`workflow_state` + the agents-SDK housekeeping tables (`cf_agents_state`/`cf_agents_schedules`/`cf_agents_queues`/`cf_agents_mcp_servers`), `ctx.storage.deleteAll()`. `PortalIndex` tracks session instance names under `session:{workflowId}:{sessionId}` (`addSession`/`deleteSessions`) - `portal.ts:openSession` registers on init, best-effort. `CloudService.removeWorkflow` hits `/workflow/purge`; `purgeIfDeployed` wraps it for the library-delete path (refresh status, purge if `hasWorkflow`, never throws, warns on failure). Wired into BOTH `WorkflowsPanel.remove` and the `workflow_delete` studio-action executor. DI: `CloudService` injects `WorkflowService` (not the reverse), so cleanup orchestration lives in the component/action, NOT in `WorkflowService.removeFromLibrary` (kept storage-pure). Connection secrets in `SecretVault` left intact (shared across workflows); D1 `usage` rows retained (billing). CORS preflight already allowed `DELETE` so no `index.ts` change for the method. Test: `cloud/test/portal-cleanup.test.mjs`.
- 2026-08-11 - GOTCHA (agents SDK inter-DO calls): do NOT use `stub.fetch(url)` to call another `WorkflowAgent` instance - the `agents` SDK's `routeAgentRequest` router needs the full `/agents/workflow-agent/{instance}/` prefix and the auth layer, so a bare internal URL 500s. Use RPC instead: `this.env.WorkflowAgent.get(id) as unknown as { methodName(...): Promise<...> }` then `await stub.methodName(...)` - the SDK exposes public methods as RPC automatically (existing pattern: `acceptPortalRun`). Used this for `purgeSelf(cascade)` (session DOs are purged via `stub.purgeSelf(false)` from the owner).
- 2026-08-11 - GOTCHA (agents SDK `ctx.storage.deleteAll`): `this.ctx.storage` IS accessible on `Agent` subclasses (the SDK itself uses it: `this.ctx.storage.sql`, `deleteAlarm`, `deleteAll` in its own `destroy()`). But `deleteAll()` only clears the DO's KEY-VALUE storage, NOT the SQLite tables - the SDK's state lives in `cf_agents_state` (SQLite), so a purge must `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS cf_agents_state`/`cf_agents_schedules`/`cf_agents_queues`/`cf_agents_mcp_servers` separately or those rows leak. The SDK's own `destroy()` drops them but also calls `this.ctx.abort("destroyed")` (via setTimeout) which aborts the request context - do NOT call `destroy()` from an HTTP handler that needs to return a response; replicate its table drops + `deleteAll()` instead.
- 2026-08-11 - GOTCHA (CORS on SDK 404/405): `routeAgentRequest` (agents SDK) returns its own Response for unknown methods/paths WITHOUT CORS headers, so the browser blocks the body and the studio sees a misleading CORS error instead of the real 404. Fixed in `cloud/src/index.ts` by attaching the studio CORS headers to every response leaving the handler (not just the `??` fallback). Always check this when a new route 404s in the browser but works via curl.
- 2026-08-11 - "Deployed to cloud" status indicator: `WorkflowSpec` has no `deployed` field, and `CloudService.deployedStatus` is a single signal for the ACTIVE workflow only (populated by `refreshStatus`, called only when the Cloud dialog opens). For a per-library-workflow badge without N network round-trips, use the local `WorkflowVersion.deployed?: boolean` flag (set by `WorkflowVersionsService.recordDeploy` on push). Added `WorkflowVersionsService.deployedWorkflowIds` signal (a `ReadonlySet<string>`) backed by a single IndexedDB scan on startup (`IndexedDbStorageService.listDeployedWorkflowIds` - full-table scan of `workflow-versions` store, filters `deployed: true`) and updated incrementally: `recordDeploy` adds, `deleteForWorkflow`/`CloudService.removeWorkflow` (purge) removes via `unmarkDeployed`. The toolbar cloud icon (`toolbar.ts` `cloudDeployed` computed) prefers the live `deployedStatus` when checked, falls back to the local set; the workflow card badge (`workflows-panel.html`) uses the local set only. Both styled with `--phorma-accent-green`. Note: the local flag reflects "has been deployed", not "is currently deployed" - the Cloud dialog's `refreshStatus` corrects the live state for the active workflow.
- 2026-08-07 - Overlay z-index bug: `.phorma-confirm` (ConfirmDialogService's dialog) was `z-index: 80`, TIED with every real dialog (`.phorma-cloud`, settings, connection-editor, etc., also 80). A confirm summoned from inside a real dialog (e.g. Cloud dialog's "Remove from cloud") lost the tie to DOM order and rendered behind it. Fixed by bumping `.phorma-confirm` to `85` (steering doc `conventions.md` updated: 75 expanded panels / 80 real dialogs / 85 confirm / 90 command palette). Any new "always on top of any dialog" surface needs its own tier here, not a reused value.
- 2026-08-07 - CREDENTIALS THAT REACH A DEPLOYED WORKER - the honest matrix, verified by reading every path. A deployed run can ONLY resolve a credential that exists as a worker secret: `CONN_<ID>_<KEY>` (connections) or `MCP_<AUTHKEY>` (remote MCP bearer, now a declared `MCP_${string}` index signature on `Env` instead of a `as keyof Env` cast). Consequences: (a) stdio MCP is impossible by design; (b) interactive-OAuth MCP is impossible in the cloud in BOTH modes - tokens live in the studio keychain via `mcp-oauth.service.ts` `mcp-oauth:{nodeId}` and `CloudToolHost.mcpFor` only ever reads `authKey`, never `authMode`. **UPDATED 2026-08-10: point (c) no longer holds for `CONN_*` - see the SecretVault entry below. It still holds for `MCP_*`, so a remote MCP node with an `authKey` in hosted mode still runs UNAUTHENTICATED and fails silently at the MCP server.**
- 2026-08-10 - CONNECTION SECRETS ON A DEPLOYED RUN, second ingestion path (`SecretVault`, spec `.kiro/specs/deployed-credential-vault/`). The reported bug: save a bearer secret in the connection editor, push to the cloud, get "Connection X is missing 1 of 1 secret values on Cloudflare Worker" and an aborted push. Correct behaviour, unactionable UX - the local value is in the OS keychain (`conn:{id}:{key}`) and the worker counts `CONN_*` env vars, and nothing in the app could set one. Now: `POST /api/connection-secrets {connectionId, secretKey, value}` encrypts with `KEY_ENC_SECRET` and stores in a `SecretVault` DO scoped `secrets:{userId}` (hosted) / `secrets:default` (BYO); `WorkerConnectionStore` reads env FIRST, vault second. Gotchas that bit or nearly bit: (a) the vault must be per OWNER not per workflow, or the operator re-enters the same key once per workflow; (b) `pushWorkflow` reads the inventory BEFORE `POST /workflow` stamps `ownerId`, so `connectionHost` needs an `ownerFallback` from `auth.userId` or a hosted tenant's FIRST deploy of a workflow reads the wrong vault and reports everything missing; (c) a new DO class needs migration `v3` in `wrangler.jsonc` top level AND `env.hosted` AND `DeployConfigService.DO_MIGRATIONS`/`DO_BINDINGS` - the generated `wrangler.byo.jsonc` REPLACES the committed config, so missing it silently drops the binding from every BYO deploy; (d) the route sits ABOVE the `store.enabled` gate in `api.ts` because BYO has no D1; (e) it refuses on a BYO worker with neither `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` nor `PHORMA_TOKEN` - an open worker treats every caller as owner, fine for `/trigger`, not for a credential store. `deploy-config.test.mjs` now derives the expected DO class list from `src/index.ts`'s export statement, so this class of drift fails a test instead of a deploy.
- 2026-08-11 - The vault shipped with a DEAD END in the connection editor, reported by a user on a `basic` (user + password) HTTP connection: both the local-save button and the cloud-upload button deleted the row's draft on success, and both were disabled without a draft. So whichever store you wrote first, the other one became unreachable for that value - and since NEITHER store can be read back, "sync the stored value" is not a thing that can exist. Symptom as reported: saved the secrets locally, cloud upload greyed out, push kept aborting with "missing 2 of 2 secret values". Fix: `saveSecret` fans out from the ONE draft to every store this install has (keychain when `secretsSupported`, deploy target when `cloudConfigured()`), and the draft survives until every one of them holds it (`secretMissingSomewhere`). Phorma Cloud consent is asked once per DIALOG session (`cloudConsent` signal, reset in `seedForm`) instead of once per secret, or a two-secret auth mode stacks two identical prompts; declining stores locally and keeps the draft so the explicit cloud button is still a way in. `putConnectionSecret` grew a `{silent}` option so the fan-out reports both stores in one toast - errors always toast. Lesson for any write-only store: never clear the only copy of a value while a second destination still needs it. Test: `connection-editor-dialog.spec.ts`.
- 2026-08-10 - The connection editor asked for the same secret name TWICE - once as `auth.secretKey` (a pointer) and once as a declared field in the Secrets list - with nothing linking them, so a typo resolved to nothing at run time with no visible cause. Fixed by `authSecretKeyNames(auth)` (engine) + `withAuthSecretKeys` (editor): saving a connection auto-declares every name the selected auth mode points at. ADD-ONLY on purpose - removing a name the operator stopped pointing at would orphan a stored value. Do not "clean up" `secretKeys` to match auth.
- 2026-08-10 - `ConnectionSummary.missingSecretKeys` (both stores populate it) + `HostCapabilities.connectionSecretScheme` (`os-keychain` | `cloudflare-worker-env` | `none`) are what make a missing-secret finding end in an action naming the exact entry. The scheme is DECLARED data, not an inferred host id, so a new host inherits no remedy text by accident. Keep the finding's `(secret keys: ...)` fragment: `capabilities-findings.spec.ts` asserts on it.
- 2026-08-07 - `smtp` is a DECLARED BUT UNIMPLEMENTED `ConnectionType`. It is in `ALL_CONNECTION_TYPES` and therefore in every host's `connectionTypes` (so push validation lets it through), and the connection editor offers it, but nothing anywhere speaks SMTP: no `lettre` in Cargo.toml, zero `smtp` matches in `cloud/src/` or `backend/src-tauri/src/`, and `engine.ts` says outright it "keeps an SMTP client out of the engine". The `notify` node's `email` channel is an HTTPS POST to a provider API (`notifyUrl`/`baseUrl`), rejecting any non-http(s) URL. Email from the cloud = transactional API (Resend/SendGrid/Postmark) over an `http` connection, never SMTP.
- 2026-08-07 - Deploy-target findings: `CapabilityFindingsService` validated ONLY against the local host, so an undeployable node (stdio MCP being the canonical case) looked perfectly fine on the canvas and first failed at push, after the workflow was fully built. Now `localFindings` (unchanged severity, still gates local runs via `RunControllerService`) + `deployFindings` (validated against `CLOUDFLARE_CAPABILITIES`, forced to `warning`, tagged `deployOnly: true`, deduped against local messages by message text, suppressed when `cloudProvider() === null`) and `findings` = both. `deployOnly` MUST stay a warning - these fire while the author is iterating locally and must never block a local run. The canvas popover renders a "DEPLOY" tag for them.
- 2026-08-07 - PALETTE BUG (pre-existing, found by E2E): searching any MCP server name ("jira", "resend") returned "No nodes match your search". MCP presets render INSIDE the Tools group's `<section>`, but `sections()` dropped any group with `entries.length === 0` - and a preset-name query matches no CATALOG entry, so Tools vanished and took every preset with it. The Tools group must survive when `mcpPresets()` is non-empty. Regression test: `agents-palette.spec.ts`. Lesson: whenever a group's template renders extra content beyond `entries`, its empty-check has to account for that content.
- 2026-08-07 - MCP transport is now shown as an ICON, never spelled into labels (`node-catalog.spec.ts` pins that no preset label contains "(local"/"(remote"). Shared helpers in `node-catalog.ts`: `mcpTransportKind(transport)` (absent/`stdio` -> `local`, `sse` -> `remote` - matching `defaultData()`, and getting this backwards would mark every generic MCP node deployable), `MCP_LOCAL_ICON` (`ti ti-device-desktop`), `MCP_TRANSPORT_LABEL`, and `MCP_TRANSPORT_CANVAS_ICON`. Remote uses the `app-phorma-cloud-icon` SVG in the DOM, but Canvas2D paints from the icon FONT and cannot use an SVG component - hence the separate `MCP_TRANSPORT_CANVAS_ICON` map (`ti ti-cloud`). Rendered in: palette sub-group headings + per-tile pip, properties "MCP server" label, Settings Integrations card title, and the canvas kind badge (`transportGlyph`/`transportFont` on `RendererNode`, painted inside the same pill left of the `mcp-tool` text, with `bw` widened by `transportW` or the text overflows the pill).
- 2026-08-07 - Settings -> Integrations filtered on `envSchema.length > 0`, which silently EXCLUDED every OAuth preset (an OAuth credential is an interactive session, so `envSchema` is empty). The canvas warning's "Configure in Settings - Integrations" deep-link (`#integration-{presetId}`) then landed on a page with no trace of the server it was complaining about - the reported "I don't see it in the list". Filter is now `envSchema.length > 0 || authMode === 'oauth'`, and OAuth cards carry a note pointing at the node's Connect button. `node-catalog.spec.ts` pins that every OAuth preset and every `remoteAlternativeId` target is listed. Any new preset-warning source needs a matching Integrations entry or its deep-link is a dead end.
- 2026-08-07 - `pTooltip` silently does NOTHING if the component's `imports` lacks `TooltipModule` (PrimeNG directives are per-component in standalone Angular). `PropertiesForm` does not import it, so the transport pill there uses a native `title` instead; `SettingsDialog` does import it, so `pTooltip` is fine in that template. Check the component's `imports` before reaching for a PrimeNG directive in its template.
- 2026-08-07 - `angular.json` `anyComponentStyle` warning is 22kB / error 26kB (raised from 20/24 for the settings dialog's Integrations group expanders). The committed `settings-dialog.scss` was ALREADY ~20.2kB compiled before that change - it lives permanently at the warning line. Convention (from this and the prior 12kB->18kB bump): consolidate duplicated selectors FIRST, then bump the budget only for the residual, leaving headroom to the error cap. Do NOT treat this as licence to grow every component - it is scoped to a legitimately dense settings surface.
- 2026-08-07 - Integrations now groups servers into collapsible `<details>` expanders (`Remote MCP servers` / `Local MCP servers`, remote first, count pill, chevron rotates via `details[open] > .caret`). The Local/Remote tag FLOATS RIGHT of the card's head flex row (it is the third child of `__integration-head`, after icon + text), not inline in the `<h5>` - inline made it wrap under long descriptions. Deep-linked cards auto-expand their collapsed group: the anchor-scroll effect does `target.closest('details').open = true` BEFORE `scrollIntoView`, because a card inside a closed expander is display:none and unscrollable. Integration cards dropped their own border/padding (the group `<details>` is the bordered container now); stacked cards separate with a top border on the `+` sibling.
- 2026-08-07 - `.phorma-settings__hint` is indented to the field-label column (`$settings-row-indent`), so it is WRONG for a card-level note - it renders visually detached under the description. Added `.phorma-settings__integration-note` (no indent) for notes that belong to the integration card rather than a credential row.
- 2026-08-07 - `McpPreset.remoteAlternativeId` links a stdio preset to its remote twin so a deploy warning can name the fix ("Swap it for X"). Enrichment happens in `CapabilityFindingsService.withRemedy`, NOT the engine - `MCP_PRESETS` is studio data and the engine must stay catalog-free. Added `atlassian-remote` (`https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp/authv2`, OAuth, supports dynamic client registration so no `oauthSetup` needed) and `email-remote` (Resend `https://mcp.resend.com/mcp`, deliberately BEARER not OAuth because bearer is the only thing a deployed worker can resolve). Renamed the stdio ones to "Jira (local)"/"Email (local)". `node-catalog.spec.ts` pins that every `remoteAlternativeId` resolves to an existing `sse` preset with a URL.
- 2026-08-07 - LOST-UPDATE BUG (root cause of "MCP email credentials don't stick"): `refreshMcpSecretFlagsScoped` did `const next = {...this.mcpSecretsConfigured()}` -> `await` N `has_secret` IPC calls -> `.set(next)`. `GraphCanvas.mcpCredentialRefresher` fires node-scope AND preset-scope refreshes for every MCP node in one unawaited block, so several always overlap and the last to resolve discarded the others' flags. The keychain value was fine the whole time; only the flag map lost it, and re-saving (one uncontended refresh) appeared to fix it until next launch. Fix: build a local delta and `.update(current => ({...current, ...resolved}))`. Extracted `hasMcpSecret(scope, envKey)` so `settings.service.spec.ts` can stub it with per-key delays - WITHOUT staggered delays the bug is invisible, because browser mode resolves synchronously and every refresh lands in one microtask. Any signal holding a shared map that async writers touch needs `update`, never `set`.
- 2026-08-10 - TYPO DOMAIN FIXED: the hosted default was `https://dev.phoma-labs.com` (no `r`) - deployed before `phorma-labs.com` was registered, then left. `PHORMA_CLOUD_DEFAULT_URL` is now `https://cloud.phorma-labs.com` and lives in the new leaf module `core/phorma-cloud-url.ts` with `loadPhormaCloudUrl()` / `savePhormaCloudUrl()`. Changing the constant alone was NOT enough: the settings dialog persists whatever it resolved, so installs carry the old host in `phorma.layout.phormaCloudUrl` and would keep using it forever. `loadPhormaCloudUrl()` compares by HOST against `LEGACY_HOSTS` and rewrites + re-persists on read. Keep `dev.phoma-labs.com` serving until the fleet updates; the updater endpoint is a `workers.dev` host, so updates do not depend on either custom domain. `ng build` (not `tsc`) caught that removing the `loadLayout` import from `model-transport.service.ts` broke two unrelated Ollama/LM Studio call sites in the same file.
- 2026-08-10 - Public status route `cloud/src/status.ts` (`/status.json`, `/status.svg`) for phorma-labs.com. Details in the `cloud-worker` steering. Two things that cost time: (1) `Env.WorkflowAgent` is an UNTYPED `DurableObjectNamespace`, so `StatusEnv` must declare it untyped too and narrow at the call site with `as unknown as` - typing it `DurableObjectNamespace<WorkflowAgent>` makes `env as StatusEnv` in `index.ts` a TS2352 error; `PortalIndex` is typed and must stay typed. (2) A tsx test that transitively imports `portal-registry.ts` or `secret-vault.ts` cannot resolve `cloudflare:workers`. Fix used in `status.test.mjs`: `registerHooks` from `node:module` redirecting that specifier to `test/stubs/cloudflare-workers.mjs`, then `await import()` the module under test - the hook must be registered before the graph loads. Reuse that shim for any future unit test touching a DO module.
- 2026-08-11 - `ctx.storage.deleteAll()` IS NOT SAFE in a SQLite-backed Durable Object that keeps serving. On SQLite DOs it deletes the TABLES, not just key-value pairs, so the still-live instance loses `cf_agents_state` and `cf_agents_schedules`: the `setState` at the end of `WorkflowAgent.purgeSelf` threw "no such table" (the purge reported failure after doing the work) and a second purge threw from the SDK's `getSchedules()`. It also does NOT delete the Durable Object, so it buys nothing - the purge path now just empties rows and calls `deleteAlarm()`. Related: `DELETE FROM x` throws when `x` was never created (`cf_agents_queues`, `cf_agents_mcp_servers` are lazy), and a tagged-template value cannot be a table identifier, so filter through `SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'` and keep the table names literal.
- 2026-08-11 - NEVER re-wrap a response from `routeAgentRequest` without excluding WebSocket upgrades. A CORS-attachment block in `index.ts` rebuilt every response missing `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, which caught the 101 upgrade: `new Response(body, init)` drops the `webSocket` handle and workerd rejects status 101, so the cloud monitor could not connect at all. The SDK's own CORS helper skips upgrades for exactly this reason. Every `WorkflowAgent.json()` response already carries CORS, so only the SDK's own 404/405 needed it.
- 2026-08-11 - Portal session Durable Objects are only reachable through the `PortalIndex` session registry (`session:{workflowId}:{sessionId}`) - a DO namespace cannot be enumerated. So teardown is `listSessions` then `forgetSessions`, and a session is forgotten ONLY after its DO is purged; deleting the key first (the original `deleteSessions`) guaranteed a permanent orphan on any failure. `purgeSelf` returns `orphanedSessions` for that reason. `openSession` runs on EVERY visitor turn, so its registry write goes out in a `Promise.all` with `initPortalSession` rather than serially.
- 2026-08-11 - The studio's cloud status signals (`deployedStatus` / `deployedStatusWorkflowId`) are ONE shared slot, so read them through `CloudService.deployedStatusFor(workflowId)`. `purgeIfDeployed` (library delete) checks a workflow that is usually not the open one; when it wrote those signals the Cloud dialog rendered the deleted workflow's status as the active workflow's. Same class of bug in toasts: use the id-resolved name, not `workflow.activeName()`.
- 2026-08-11 - `cloud/test/deploy-validation.test.mjs` is the ONLY harness with a real Durable Object (wrangler `--dry-run` bundle run under Miniflare), so worker-route regressions belong there rather than in a new file that pays the bundle cost again. It caught `DELETE /workflow/purge` shipping with `purgeSelf(false)` - the cascade (cron, portal unpublish, session purge) never ran. Prove a cascade through the portal slug: it lives in a DIFFERENT DO, so it can only disappear if the owner really cascaded. `mf.dispatchFetch(url, { headers: { Upgrade: 'websocket' } })` tests the upgrade path; call `accept()` before `close()` or workerd throws.
- 2026-08-24 - The telemetry admin aggregates (`cloud/src/telemetry-admin.ts`) are reachable as `aggregateTelemetry(route, range, db)`, deliberately split from `handleTelemetryAdminRequest`: the authorization gate needs a real Clerk session (an open BYO instance resolves `userId: null`, which the allowlist rejects with 403), so the SQL can only be exercised through the pure-ish core. Miniflare's D1 is real SQLite, so `json_extract` and `json_each` both work - a `d1Databases` binding plus `mf.getD1Database('DB')` under `tsx` is enough to test the aggregation without building the worker bundle. The summary route's trailing d1/d7/d30 windows are CLAMPED to the requested range, otherwise `d30` on a 3-day range reads rows the caller did not ask for and "rows outside the range contribute nothing" stops holding.
- 2026-08-24 - `admin/`'s Admin_API client (`core/telemetry-api.service.ts`) makes "request without a bearer token" unrepresentable rather than policed: the token funnels through a branded `SessionToken` that only `toSessionToken` mints from a non-blank string, and the single private `send()` requires one, so the no-session early return is the only other path (10.2, 10.3). The resolver sits behind the `SESSION_TOKEN_RESOLVER` injection token so a test can substitute it. ngx-clerk gotchas behind that: `ClerkService.session$` / `clerk$` are `ReplaySubject`s that NEVER emit while the publishable key is the placeholder, so track the latest emission and treat "not yet emitted" as no session - awaiting them hangs the app; and `ClerkService` exposes no `signOut`, so sign out goes through the instance from `clerk$`. The sign-in surface mounts ngx-clerk's own `<clerk-sign-in />` (selector `clerk-sign-in`, standalone). `admin/src/styles.scss` needed its own copy of `.phorma-btn-content` - it shares no stylesheet with `frontend/`, so solid `pButton` labels paint invisible without it.
- 2026-08-24 - The five `admin/` views share ONE presentational rail (`views/view-state-rail.ts`) for loading, empty and failed, and one `views/group-table.ts` for every grouped aggregate. Each view is `@if (loaded(); as data) { ...markup... } @else { <admin-view-state [state]="state()" (retry)="reload()" /> }`, which is what makes "exactly one of the four states" structural: the rail renders nothing when loaded, and its three states are arms of one `@switch`. Do NOT project loaded markup through `<ng-content>` inside the rail - projected content is instantiated with the parent template, so its bindings evaluate even when the branch is not rendered. Every state carries `data-view-state="<kind>"`, so counting `[data-view-state]` is a direct exclusivity assertion. Two typing traps: a declared interface such as `FeatureRow` or `TrendDay` has no implicit index signature and is NOT assignable to `GroupRow`, so rebuild rows as object literals; and `Record<TelemetryRoute, () => Promise<unknown>>` does not satisfy `loadComponent`, use `NonNullable<Route['loadComponent']>`. Trend excludes the k-anonymity `other` row from the plot (a non-date on a time axis) but still lists it in the day table, so no reported label is hidden, and its chart options are a `computed()` because `suggestedMax` comes from loaded data. Lazy-routing the five views plus `@defer (on immediate)` on `<p-chart>` keeps chart.js in its own 207kB `primeng-chart` chunk: initial bundle 785kB against a 1.5MB warning.
- 2026-08-25 - Angular 20 `resource().value()` THROWS (`ResourceValueError`) while the resource is in its error state, so `viewStateOf({ loading: r.isLoading(), error: r.error(), value: r.value() })` throws during change detection on any failed request instead of resolving to `failed` - the object literal evaluates `value` eagerly, so the precedence inside `viewStateOf` never gets a chance. All five `admin/` views shipped with that bare read and their failed state plus retry control never rendered; the guard is `value: r.hasValue() ? r.value() : undefined` (`hasValue()` is false in the error state and stays false through a reload from it). Found by `admin/src/app/views/views.spec.ts`, which asserts `[data-view-state]` count across all four states. Harness notes from that file: answering a request needs TWO rounds of `detectChanges()` + a macrotask (the first delivers the answer to the resource, the second renders the state), the trend mounts run with `DeferBlockBehavior.Manual` so a 100-iteration property does not load and tear down chart.js each time (the plot is asserted on `chartData()`, since `UIChart` paints into a canvas with nothing readable in the DOM), and generated group labels must be whitespace-free and distinct - `GroupTable` tracks `@for` by label, so a duplicate is an Angular error rather than a view defect.
- 2026-08-25 - `cloud/test/telemetry-ingest.test.mjs` runs the wrangler `--dry-run` bundle under Miniflare behind a small harness MODULE (`modulesRoot` + two `ESModule` entries, the harness re-exporting `WorkflowAgent`, `PortalIndex` and `SecretVault` from the bundle so the DO bindings still resolve). That wrapper is what makes three otherwise unobservable claims assertable: a proxied `env.DB` records every SQL string and BOUND VALUE (needed for "no marker in any write" and for write COUNTS), `console.*` is reassigned inside the isolate so "no log line leaks" is real, and `Date.now` is driven by an `x-test-now-ms` header so the rolling rate window, `first_seen_at` and the 400 day retention edge are exact. Failure injection is a `/__t/fail` route that rejects any `batch()` whose SQL starts with a given prefix. Do NOT reset the module-level `ensureTelemetrySchema` guard: one warm-up ingest creates the schema and the SQL it issued IS the real `TELEMETRY_SCHEMA_STATEMENTS` and prune statements, captured instead of copied. Property tests replaying one Install_Id must clear `telemetry_ingest_rate` between iterations, or shrinking hits the 20/hour 429 and stops exercising the write path.
- 2026-08-25 - A Clerk-authorized Worker route CAN be tested end to end under Miniflare with no Clerk account and no stub: generate an RSA keypair in the test, bind the public PEM as `CLERK_JWT_KEY` (plus any non-empty `CLERK_SECRET_KEY`, which only selects the branch), and sign RS256 JWTs with the private half. `@clerk/backend` then verifies OFFLINE - no JWKS fetch, real `verifyRequest`, real allowlist check. Constraints: the key must be **RSA 2048 with exponent 65537** because `loadClerkJwkFromPem` extracts the modulus by string-stripping the standard SPKI prefix/suffix; the payload needs `sub`, `iat`, `nbf`, `exp`; and `exp`/`iat` are checked against the in-isolate `Date.now`, so mint them around the harness's virtual clock, not the wall clock. This is what makes the 200/400/404/405/500 answers of `/api/admin/telemetry/*` reachable in `cloud/test/telemetry-admin.test.mjs` - an open BYO worker only ever reaches 401 and 403, because `verifyRequest` hands an anonymous context (null `userId`) to a worker with no secrets and a null id is never allowlisted. Two more traps there: an `OPTIONS` request never reaches the Admin_API (the generic CORS branch in `index.ts` sits above the `/api/*` chain), so it is out of scope for "every admin response carries `Cache-Control: no-store`"; and a FLAT cross product of routes x methods x tokens x ranges almost never produces a 200 or a 404, because 401 and 403 swallow any method and any tail - generate the ANSWER CLASS first, then an input that produces it, and assert the expected status alongside the header.
- 2026-08-26 - `cloud`'s `test:unit` chain now runs FOUR Miniflare suites back to back and `telemetry-ingest` flaked once at iteration 94 with `TypeError: fetch failed -> connect EADDRINUSE 127.0.0.1:<port>`. Cause is the harness, not the worker: `Miniflare#dispatchFetch` sets `reset: true` on every runtime request (`DispatchFetchDispatcher.dispatch`), so its internal undici `Pool` never keeps a connection alive - one request, one socket, 120s in TIME_WAIT on Windows. Measured 8.9k to 12.7k sockets in TIME_WAIT across consecutive chains against a ~16k ephemeral range. A keep-alive dispatcher is NOT reachable from the test: `dispatchFetch` overwrites `init.dispatcher` with its own before calling undici, so any agent you pass is discarded, and rebuilding the request by hand means reproducing miniflare's internal `MF-Original-URL` / CF-blob headers. The fix is `withLoopbackRetry` (`cloud/test/miniflare-loopback.mjs`), which patches `dispatchFetch` on the instance so every call site is covered by one edit at the worker factory, and retries ONLY an error whose cause chain carries `EADDRINUSE`/`EADDRNOTAVAIL` on a replayable (string or absent) body. Safe because a connect failure happens before any byte reaches workerd, so a retry cannot double-write; `ECONNRESET` is deliberately NOT retried (it can mean workerd died). Do not solve this by lowering `numRuns` - the floor is 100.
- 2026-08-25 - `corsHeaders` in `cloud/src/index.ts` answers an UNLISTED origin with the FIRST entry of `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` (`list.includes(o) ? o : list[0]`), not with no header and not with `*`. So a new browser origin does not fail as "CORS header missing" - it fails as "Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://localhost:7322 does not match", which reads like a misconfigured client. The admin dashboard's dev server (7323) needed adding to that list under `env.hosted` next to the studio's 7322; the list change only reaches production on a `wrangler deploy --env hosted`, but a local `wrangler dev --env hosted` picks it up immediately from the committed config.
- 2026-08-25 - Verify what the HOSTED worker is actually running before debugging an authorization or route problem against it. `GET /status.json` reports `build` (the package version) and its component list, and `OPTIONS /telemetry` reveals route order: an `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` of the `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` head instead of `*` means the request fell through to the generic OPTIONS branch, so the telemetry routes are not in that build. Caught the hosted worker sitting on `0.2.0-beta.9` with eight status components (no `telemetry` store) while the repo was on beta.10 - `/api/admin/telemetry/*` answered a bodiless 404 and D1 migration `0002_telemetry.sql` was still unapplied, so setting `TELEMETRY_ADMIN_USER_IDS` alone would have changed nothing.
- 2026-08-26 - "No telemetry in the admin console" was a CLIENT bug, and the way to find it was to read the installed app's real `localStorage` off disk rather than reason about the code. WebView2 keeps it at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\com.phorma.agentstudio\EBWebView\Default\Local Storage\leveldb`; read the `.ldb`/`.log` bytes as Latin-1 (`[System.Text.Encoding]::GetEncoding(28591)`) and regex for `phorma\.telemetry\.` - keys and JSON survive snappy compression well enough to read. The decisive evidence was an ABSENT key: `phorma.telemetry.upload` is written only by `applyIngestOutcome`, so no `nextAttemptAt` anywhere on disk proves no upload was ever ATTEMPTED, which rules out network, CORS, ingest URL and rejection in one step. Root cause: `defaultUploadState` armed the gate at `now + 15min` on every cold start, and since the record is not persisted until an attempt happens, every restart re-armed it - an install used in sessions shorter than 15 minutes uploaded literally never. Fixed to `now`; the gate is still re-armed after every attempt, which is what 4.3/5.4 actually require.
- 2026-08-26 - Before blaming the client for a missing-data report, prove the server half in two commands: `Invoke-WebRequest -Method Post https://cloud.phorma-labs.com/telemetry` with a valid Rollup (expect `200 {}`), then `npx wrangler d1 execute phorma-cloud --env hosted --remote --command "SELECT ... FROM telemetry_rollups"`. Delete the probe row afterwards or it shows up in the dashboard as a real install.

## MCP Presets

- 2026-07-07 — Adding an MCP preset = ONE entry in `MCP_PRESETS` (`frontend/src/app/core/node-catalog.ts`). The palette, properties panel, settings-dialog Integrations, node instantiation, and the Rust stdio spawn path all pick it up automatically. No backend/model changes for stdio npx/uvx presets (Rust `resolve_command` already handles npx + uvx).
- 2026-07-07 — Presets needing a non-secret positional ARG (e.g. filesystem allowed dir) use `argFields?: McpArgField[]`. They're appended as trailing positional args after the static `args` in `mcpPresetToCatalogEntry` and rendered as labeled inputs in the properties panel via the `mcpArgFields` computed (field + absolute index into `data.args`). Don't confuse with `envSchema` (secrets, keychain).
- 2026-07-07 — Settings › Integrations only lists presets with `envSchema.length > 0` (filtered in settings-dialog.ts `mcpPresets`). No-secret presets (filesystem/git/fetch/memory/sequential-thinking) would otherwise render empty cards.
- 2026-07-07 — The `sse`/remote "Server URL" input ALREADY EXISTS in properties-panel.html (the `@else` branch of `transport === 'stdio'`). Don't rebuild it when adding remote-transport presets. Preset credential fields (bearer token) render in that same `@else` when `mcpPreset()` is truthy.
- 2026-07-07 — Remote (`sse`) MCP presets: set `transport:'sse'`, `url`, and `authKey` (the envSchema field name whose secret becomes `Authorization: Bearer <token>`). `command`/`args` stay required by the `McpPreset` type — set them to `''`/`[]`. `mcpPresetToCatalogEntry` branches sse vs stdio for defaultData.
- 2026-07-07 — REMOTE MCP BEARER AUTH crosses the trust boundary differently than stdio. stdio secrets stay in Rust (injected as env vars). A remote bearer token must reach the HTTP request in the webview, so `HttpMcpClient(endpoint, authHeaders)` takes headers and the CALLER resolves the token (keeps engine framework-free). Desktop: narrow Rust command `mcp::get_mcp_bearer(server_id, auth_key, preset_id)` returns ONLY that one secret (node-scoped then preset-scoped). Browser: `SettingsService.resolveMcpBearer` reads localStorage. Cloud: `CloudToolHost({resolveBearer})` maps authKey -> worker secret `MCP_<AUTHKEY>` (e.g. `GITHUB_TOKEN` -> `MCP_GITHUB_TOKEN`).
- 2026-07-07 — `ToolHostService.httpMcpFor` is ASYNC (resolves the bearer before constructing the client). Both call sites (`listMcpTools`, `callMcpTool`) must `await (await this.httpMcpFor(...))`.
- 2026-07-07 — Shipped remote bearer preset: GitHub (`https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/`, authKey `GITHUB_TOKEN` = PAT). REMOVED Pipedream + Composio: they don't fit a static bearer (Pipedream needs a client-credentials token exchange + per-request `x-pd-*` headers at `remote.mcp.pipedream.net/v3`, one app per connection; Composio generates per-session `mcp.url`+headers via its SDK, no static endpoint). Both are OAuth/session-shaped — Phase 3+ territory, not a one-field preset.
- 2026-07-07 — INTERACTIVE MCP OAUTH (Phase 3) is split by trust boundary: pure logic in `engine/src/mcp-oauth.ts` (`McpOAuthClient`: RFC9728/RFC8414 discovery, RFC7591 DCR, PKCE S256, RFC8707 resource param, code exchange, refresh — injected `OAuthCrypto`+fetch, no DOM). Host wiring in `frontend/src/app/core/mcp-oauth.service.ts` (`McpOAuthService`). Desktop consent = Rust loopback in `backend/src-tauri/src/oauth.rs` (`oauth_loopback_start`/`_wait`/`_cancel`, `std::net::TcpListener` on `127.0.0.1:0`). Browser consent = popup + `postMessage` from static `frontend/public/oauth/callback.html` (redirect `origin/oauth/callback.html`). Loopback chosen over custom scheme (spec allows localhost + pairs with DCR).
- 2026-07-07 — `McpToolData.authMode: 'bearer'|'oauth'` selects the auth path in `ToolHostService.httpMcpFor`: `oauth` -> `McpOAuthService.validAccessToken` (auto-refresh, 60s skew); else `authKey` -> `resolveMcpBearer`. OAuth sessions stored under secret key `mcp-oauth:{nodeId}` (keychain desktop / localStorage browser), NEVER in workflow JSON.
- 2026-07-07 — Web Crypto `subtle.digest` under TS strict rejects `Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike>` as BufferSource — copy into a fresh `ArrayBuffer` first (see `browserCrypto()` in mcp-oauth.service.ts).
- 2026-07-07 — OAuth presets: "GitHub (OAuth)" (`github-oauth`, authMode oauth, has `oauthSetup`) alongside "GitHub (token)" (PAT), plus generic "Remote MCP (OAuth)" (`remote-mcp-oauth`, empty url, DCR path). Deployed cloud runs still use the Phase 2 `MCP_<AUTHKEY>` worker-secret bearer path (interactive OAuth token reuse in cloud not yet wired). `McpPreset.command`/`args` are OPTIONAL now (sse presets omit them).
- 2026-07-07 — MCP OAuth on desktop MUST route HTTP through Rust `http_request` (webview blocks cross-origin fetch to auth servers → "HTTP unreachable"). `McpOAuthService` passes a `routedFetch` into `McpOAuthClient` (arrow fn, so the engine's `.bind(globalThis)` is a harmless no-op). `http_request` now also returns response `headers` (lower-cased) so the 401 `WWW-Authenticate` discovery hint survives.
- 2026-07-07 — RFC 9728/8414 well-known discovery inserts `.well-known/<type>` BETWEEN host and path: for `https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp` it's `…/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` (path-aware), with root + OIDC `openid-configuration` fallbacks. Root-only 404s.
- 2026-07-07 — GitHub's OAuth AS does NOT support dynamic client registration, and GitHub OAuth apps require a FIXED callback URL. So: (a) desktop loopback prefers a STABLE port (7328) via `oauth_loopback_start(preferredPort)` with ephemeral fallback, and (b) `McpOAuthService.resolveClient` resolution order is user-stored client (`mcp-oauth-client:{nodeId}`) → preset `oauthSetup.defaultClient` → DCR. `fetch`+Web Crypto binding gotcha: bind default fetch to globalThis; copy Uint8Array into fresh ArrayBuffer for `subtle.digest`.
- 2026-07-07 — GitHub OAuth VERIFIED specifics (probed live): PRM at `…/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` advertises `scopes_supported` (repo, read:org, …) on the RESOURCE metadata, NOT the AS metadata — `McpOAuthService.connect` must pass `prm.scopes_supported` into the authorization request or the token has no grants. GitHub's token endpoint REQUIRES the client secret even for public clients (PKCE still binds the code — same model as GitHub's own MCP binary which bakes a public secret into the build), and returns HTTP 200 with an `error` JSON body on failure — `McpOAuthClient.tokenRequest` checks for in-body `error`/missing `access_token`.
- 2026-07-07 — OAuth preset UX: presets whose provider lacks DCR declare `oauthSetup` on `McpPreset` (`registerUrlTemplate` with `{callback}` placeholder, `needsClientSecret`, `note`, optional `defaultClient` for true one-click). The properties panel renders a numbered one-time-setup flow (open pre-filled register page → paste client id+secret) and gates Connect until a client resolves. GitHub's register URL pre-fills name/url/callback via `oauth_application[…]` query params.
- 2026-07-07 — Preset UX rules: preset-fixed `sse` URLs render as a read-only locked row (editing the GitHub endpooint only breaks it); the transport dropdown is hidden for ALL preset nodes (only generic "MCP Server" chooses); stdio preset nodes with an empty `envSchema` skip the credentials status pill (Filesystem/Git/etc. showed a bogus "Credentials missing" warning before). `ToolHostService` now throws actionable errors when an OAuth node is unconnected or a bearer preset has no token (previously silently sent no auth header → cryptic 401), and filters empty-string positional args before `mcp_connect`.
- 2026-07-07 — Email preset is `@n24q02m/better-email-mcp` (npx), single `EMAIL_CREDENTIALS` secret in `email:app-password` form (host auto-discovered). Replaced the old `email-reader` uvx server that used a confusing 4-field encrypted-password scheme.
- 2026-07-07 — Shipped stdio presets + verified sources: Filesystem/Memory/Sequential Thinking = `@modelcontextprotocol/server-*` (npx); Git/Fetch = `mcp-server-git`/`mcp-server-fetch` (uvx); Brave = `@brave/brave-search-mcp-server` (npx, v2 defaults stdio, `BRAVE_API_KEY`); Postgres = `postgres-mcp` (uvx, crystaldba, `--access-mode=restricted` for read-only, secret `DATABASE_URI`); Slack = `@zencoderai/slack-mcp-server` (npx, `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` + non-secret `SLACK_TEAM_ID`). The official servers repo ARCHIVED GitHub/Postgres/Slack/Brave — GitHub's replacement is a REMOTE HTTP server (deferred to Phase 2/3, not stdio). Slack fork is v0.0.1/~1yr stale (canonical but not active); Postgres last release ~14mo ago.
- 2026-08-07 — Tool-result cap was a bare `8000` literal in `engine/src/engine.ts` `executeToolCall`, clipping every tool result mid-payload. Slack `users.list` (and any paginated API whose cursor lives at the JSON tail) lost its `next_cursor` under the slice, so the model couldn't continue paging. Made it a named `DEFAULT_TOOL_RESULT_CAP_CHARS` (8000) + per-agent `AgentNodeData.toolResultCapChars` override (clamped to `MAX_TOOL_RESULT_CAP_CHARS` = 200000). Added to BOTH structural twins (`engine/src/types.ts` AND `frontend/src/app/core/workflow.model.ts`). UI control lives in the agent-config Reliability section (p-inputnumber, placeholder "default (8000)", max 200000) alongside the Compress toggle. The prompt-side workaround (pass `limit: 5` to Slack `users.list`) still applies when the cap isn't raised - the override just makes the cap tunable per node instead of global.
- 2026-08-10 — `DEFAULT_MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS = 8` in `engine/src/engine.ts` was run-level only (`RunOptions.maxToolRounds`). A Jira safety-net run with 14 assigned issues burned all 8 rounds on per-issue worklog checks and never reached the final Email Report step. Added per-agent `AgentNodeData.maxToolRounds` (both structural twins: `engine/src/types.ts` AND `frontend/src/app/core/workflow.model.ts`); the engine loop at `engine.ts:2650` now prefers the agent's value over the run-level option. The `agent()` template helper in `workflow-templates.ts` grew a `dataOverride?: Partial<Omit<AgentNodeData,'prompt'>>` param so templates can set `toolResultCapChars`/`maxToolRounds` without going inline. The Jira safety-net template sets `toolResultCapChars: 50000, maxToolRounds: 15`.
- 2026-08-10 — Atlassian REMOVED `POST /rest/api/3/search` (HTTP 410 Gone, not just deprecated). Replacement is `POST /rest/api/3/search/jql` (enhanced search). Request body schema is compatible (jql/fields/maxResults), only pagination changed (`startAt`/`total` -> `nextPageToken`/`isLast`). The `tpl-jira-search` node URL in `workflow-templates.ts` was updated; existing user workflows that branched from the template need the URL edited manually.
- 2026-08-10 — Jira safety-net prompt rewrite: replaced the N-per-issue-worklog-calls pattern (step 3) with a single JQL search using `worklogDate >= "<TODAY>" AND worklogDate <= "<TODAY>" AND worklogAuthor = currentUser()` - one search call instead of 14, collapses steps 2+3 into 2 rounds. Also: instruct the agent to use SINGLE quotes inside JQL string values (e.g. `status NOT IN ('QA','In QA')`) so the outer JSON string doesn't need quote escaping (models frequently produce invalid JSON trying to escape double quotes). And: explicitly require the Add Worklog `body` arg to be a JSON STRING not an object (the engine's per-param interpolation at `tools.ts:174` does `JSON.stringify` on non-strings, which double-encodes objects and Jira rejects with `INVALID_INPUT`).
- 2026-08-07 — Jira preset = `uvx mcp-atlassian` (sooperset/mcp-atlassian, MIT, 5.7k stars, 200 contributors, releases within weeks). Env: non-secret `JIRA_URL` + `JIRA_USERNAME`, secret `JIRA_API_TOKEN`. Leaving the `CONFLUENCE_*` vars out of `envSchema` is deliberate — the server auto-scopes its tool surface to whichever product is configured, so Jira-only config yields Jira-only tools. Icon `ti ti-brand-jira` exists in the Tabler webfont. Adding it required exactly ONE `MCP_PRESETS` entry: palette, properties panel, Settings › Integrations card (`id="integration-jira"`), missing-credential canvas badge, and its deep link all derive from `envSchema` with zero extra wiring. Rejected the official Atlassian remote server (`https://mcp.atlassian.com/v1/mcp/authv2`) for the default: it is OAuth-only, and OAuth presets are filtered OUT of Settings › Integrations (`envSchema.length > 0`), so it would not have satisfied a settings-driven setup flow.
- 2026-08-07 — ROOT CAUSE of "OAuth MCP node connects fine, still 401s once deployed": `CloudToolHost.mcpFor` (`cloud/src/workflow-agent.ts`) only ever reads `data.authKey` (static bearer -> `MCP_<AUTHKEY>` worker secret) — it never checked `data.authMode === 'oauth'`. An OAuth session (GitHub OAuth, `atlassian-remote`/"Jira & Confluence", `remote-mcp-oauth`) lives in the desktop keychain or browser localStorage and NEVER reaches the worker, so a deployed call goes out with NO `Authorization` header and the MCP server 401s. This was invisible at push time because `validateAgainstCapabilities` (engine/src/capabilities.ts) had a rule for stdio MCP (`stdioMcp` feature) but none for OAuth MCP. FIXED: added a 6th `HostCapabilities.features` flag `mcpOAuth` (true desktop+browser — `ToolHostService.httpMcpFor` already resolves `McpOAuthService.validAccessToken` on both — false on `CLOUDFLARE_CAPABILITIES`), a matching validation rule (mirrors the stdio one, same file), and a `CloudToolHost.listTools` throw naming the real constraint instead of the bare "HTTP 401". Adding a 6th feature flag means every `HostCapabilities` object literal needs it (only 3 exist, all in `capabilities.ts`) and `capabilities.spec.ts`'s hardcoded `FEATURE_FLAGS` array needs the new key too, or `'%s declares...all N feature flags'` fails.
- 2026-08-07 — The `atlassian-remote` ("Jira & Confluence") preset description literally claimed "Runs in the cloud, so scheduled and deployed workflows can use it" and the local `jira` preset's description told users to "use the remote ... server for scheduled workflows" — BOTH FALSE per the finding above (OAuth session never reaches the worker). Fixed both description strings. Also fixed `CapabilityFindingsService.withRemedy` (frontend/src/app/core/capability-findings.service.ts): it suggested swapping a `remoteAlternativeId` in as "the fix" without checking whether that alternative is itself OAuth (Jira's only remote alternative is) — recommending it just traded one deploy finding for the identical one on the swapped-in node. Now skips the remedy sentence when `alternative.authMode === 'oauth'`.
- 2026-08-07 — SEPARATE real bug found while investigating the above, likely why the user saw "still shows as a warning in the canvas" right after a successful Connect: `GraphCanvas.mcpCredentialRefresher` (frontend/src/app/workspace/canvas/graph-canvas.ts) only re-reads OAuth connection state when `this.graph()` changes. Connecting/disconnecting OAuth from the properties panel (`PropertiesForm.connectOAuth/disconnectOAuth`) touches no node data, so the canvas's cached `oauthConnected` map went stale until an unrelated graph edit forced a recompute. Fixed by adding `McpOAuthService.connectionChangeTick` (a signal bumped on successful connect/disconnect) and having the canvas effect track it alongside the graph. If you add another component that caches "is node X OAuth-connected" locally, track this tick too instead of polling once on selection.
- 2026-08-07 — FOLLOW-UP same day: "Remote" now means "cloud-deployable" everywhere, not just "over the network". `McpTransportKind` (node-catalog.ts) is `'local' | 'remote' | 'oauth'`; `mcpTransportKind(transport, authMode?)` takes a 2nd param and an sse+oauth preset is its own `'oauth'` kind with its own icon (`MCP_OAUTH_ICON` = `ti ti-key`, deliberately NOT the cloud glyph). Every consumer needed the split: canvas badge (`graph-to-scene.ts`), properties-panel transport pill, `agents-palette` sub-groups (now Remote / Sign-in (OAuth) / Local), Settings › Integrations groups (same 3-way, `settings-dialog.ts/.html`). Renamed `atlassian-remote` to "Jira & Confluence (OAuth)" (matches "GitHub (OAuth)"/"GitHub (token)"). Audited every `transport:'sse'` preset: `github-oauth` and `remote-mcp-oauth` were ALSO mis-bucketed as deployable "Remote" before this — only `github` (token) and `email-remote` (Resend, bearer) are genuinely deployable. `CapabilityFindingsService.withRemedy` no longer suggests a `remoteAlternativeId` swap when the alternative's `authMode === 'oauth'` (it doesn't fix deployability, it just moves the identical finding).
- 2026-08-07 — `http-tool` (engine/src/tools.ts) gained real generalization to actually make cloud-deployed API tools viable: (1) `params?: HttpToolParam[]` (name/description/required) — declaring params replaces the single `input` fallback with one named string property per entry, spliced into its own `{{name}}` token in BOTH url and body independently (needed because Jira's add-worklog endpoint needs an issue key in the url path AND a JSON body at once — one shared `{{input}}` token can't hold two different values). No `params` = old single-`{{input}}` behavior, byte-identical, so every existing node keeps working. (2) `connectionId?: string` — the HOST (studio `ToolHostService`, cloud `CloudToolHost`) resolves it and calls the SAME `applyConnectionAuth` that `http-request`/`notify` already use, so an agent-callable HTTP tool can finally carry real Basic/Bearer auth instead of a secret hardcoded into `node.data.headers` (an actual OWASP-relevant fix, not just a feature). Added `'http-tool'` to `CONNECTION_KINDS` in properties-form.ts — the EXISTING shared connection-picker section just works, no new picker UI needed. (3) new export `withConnectionBaseUrl(url, conn)` — a plain `{{baseUrl}}` string-replace convention (not template syntax) so a tool's url can read `{{baseUrl}}/rest/api/3/search` and the real site address lives once on the Connection, not copy-pasted into every node. `engine/src/tools.spec.ts` is a NEW file (tools.ts had zero test coverage before this).
- 2026-08-07 — GOTCHA: engine files are type-checked under the FRONTEND's stricter tsconfig (`noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature`) because the frontend build compiles `engine/src` directly — `engine`'s own `tsc`/vitest run does NOT catch this. A `Record<string, unknown>` cast means every property access, including WRITES (`properties.input = {...}`, not just reads), needs bracket notation (`properties['input']`) or `ng build` fails with TS4111 while `cd engine && npx vitest run` stays green. Always run frontend's `ng build` after touching `engine/src`, don't trust engine's own checks alone.
- 2026-08-07 — Shipped a second `WORKFLOW_TEMPLATES` entry, `tpl-jira-safety-net` ("Jira Time-Log Safety Net"), as the concrete proof this all works: 2 schedule triggers (cron has no timezone — Oct-Mar fires 08:00 UTC = 19:00 AEDT, Apr-Sep fires 09:00 UTC = 19:00 AEST, both hand off to the same agent so only one fires per evening), 1 agent, 4 `http-tool` nodes against Jira REST v3 (search / get-worklogs / add-worklog, `connectionId` deliberately left blank for the user to fill in), plus the `email-remote` (Resend, bearer) MCP preset for the report. A schedule-triggered run's `input` is ALWAYS `''` (`WorkflowAgent.scheduledRun()` calls `this.trigger('', undefined, 'schedule')`) and NO prompt anywhere gets a real date injected, so there's a 5th unauthenticated `http-tool` hitting `timeapi.io` (verified live before committing to it — `worldtimeapi.org`, the other well-known option, failed to even fetch) as the agent's mandatory first call for ground-truth "today". `workflow-templates.spec.ts` (NEW file, first test coverage for `workflow-templates.ts`) asserts the built spec clears `validateAgainstCapabilities` against `CLOUDFLARE_CAPABILITIES` with ZERO findings — an actual regression test for "genuinely deployable", not just a comment claiming it.
- 2026-08-07 — Test-writing gotcha (caught by the new spec, on the PRE-EXISTING IAS template too, not just the new one): the `node()` template helper stores raw port ids (`${nodeId}-${portKey}`, no suffix) but `connect()` stores connector ids WITH the `-in`/`-out` suffix appended. Comparing them as raw strings fails; use `portBaseId()` (exported from `@phorma/engine`) on the connector side first.

## Phorma Cloud Model Provider (Local-Run Inference Proxy)

- 2026-07-12 — `phorma-cloud` is a new `ModelProviderId` (added to BOTH `engine/src/types.ts` AND `frontend/src/app/core/workflow.model.ts` — keep the structural twins in sync). It routes local-run inference through the Phorma Cloud `/api/infer` proxy, billed against the tenant's subscription credits (OpenRouter runtime key). No BYO key needed. Curated models only (stored as full OpenRouter slugs): `openai/gpt-5.5`, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`, `anthropic/claude-opus-4.8`, `google/gemini-3.5-flash`.
- 2026-07-12 — `ModelTransportService.create()` returns a `CompositeModelClient` that intercepts `request.provider === 'phorma-cloud'` → `PhormaCloudModelClient` (POSTs the engine-built OpenRouter-shaped wire request to `${phormaCloudUrl}/api/infer` with the Clerk session JWT as Bearer; streams SSE back; parses with `createStreamParser({ ...request, provider: 'openrouter' })`). All other providers delegate to the existing Tauri/Fetch BYO path. The engine calls `stream()` per-node with `request.provider`, so the composite branches at runtime — no engine changes needed for the routing decision.
- 2026-07-12 — Cloud proxy `POST /api/infer` in `cloud/src/api.ts`: verifies Clerk JWT (`verifyRequest`), gates on subscription+quota via shared `resolveHostedInference()` (in `tenants.ts`), injects the tenant runtime key, forwards to OpenRouter, tees the response stream (one copy to the client, one parsed for the `usage` block), meters via `recordRun`. The tenant key NEVER leaves the worker. Security: authenticate every call + enforce quota exactly like `WorkflowAgent.trigger()` (402/429) — otherwise it exposes unauthenticated inference on the tenant's key.
- 2026-07-12 — CRITICAL GOTCHA (fixed): `/api/infer` metering (`meterInferenceStream`) reads the SECOND tee'd stream copy to extract usage AFTER the client's copy finishes. It MUST run via `ctx.waitUntil(...)`, NOT a bare `void promise.catch()`. Without waitUntil, Cloudflare tears the worker down as soon as the client finishes reading its copy → the metering promise is killed before `recordRun` writes to D1 → usage silently stays at 0 (symptom: Runs panel shows "N credits" for a run but Settings quota bar stays "0 / 1000"). Required threading `ExecutionContext` through `fetch(request, env, ctx)` → `handleApiRequest(..., ctx)` → `routeApiRequest(..., ctx)`. NEEDS WORKER REDEPLOY to take effect (`wrangler deploy --env hosted`).
- 2026-07-12 — Post-run quota refresh: `RunControllerService.finishRun()` calls `phormaCloud.refresh()` (after a 1.5s delay to let the waitUntil D1 write land) ONLY when `runUsage().phormaCloud` is true. Before this, the quota bar/account chip only refreshed on dialog-open/sign-in, so a just-completed Phorma Cloud run's spend never showed until you reopened Settings. `RunControllerService` injects `PhormaCloudService` directly — safe (no circular DI: PhormaCloudService only injects ClerkService, reads phormaCloudUrl from localStorage not CloudService).
- 2026-07-12 — CRITICAL GOTCHA (fixed): `recordRun` had a hardcoded `runs_used + 1` bump, called from BOTH `WorkflowAgent.trigger()` (correct: 1 per deployed workflow run) AND `meterInferenceStream` (the `/api/infer` local-run proxy — WRONG). Every local Phorma Cloud inference call (per agent node × per tool-call round) was inflating the monthly run count, so a few local debug runs pushed users to e.g. 7/300. Fix: `recordRun` takes `countsAsRun?: boolean` (default true); the SQL now uses `VALUES(?,?,?,?)` + `runs_used + excluded.runs_used` with a bound `runIncrement` (0 when countsAsRun=false, 1 otherwise). `/api/infer` passes `countsAsRun: false` — local runs consume CREDITS (cost) only, never the run allowance. `WorkflowAgent.trigger()` is unchanged (defaults to true). NEEDS WORKER REDEPLOY. Existing inflated `runs_used` rows in D1 don't self-correct — reset manually if needed (`UPDATE quotas SET runs_used = 0 WHERE tenant_id=? AND month=?`).
- 2026-07-12 — `OPENROUTER_SLUG_PREFIX`, `toOpenRouterModel()`, and `resolveHostedInference()` were lifted from `workflow-agent.ts` into `tenants.ts` as shared exports (the DO + the `/api/infer` proxy both use them). `mapGraphToOpenRouter` in `workflow-agent.ts` handles `phorma-cloud` nodes (prefix `''`, provider→openrouter) so deployed workflows with phorma-cloud nodes work in hosted mode. BYO own-Cloudflare deploy: phorma-cloud errors clearly (no tenant key).
- 2026-07-12 — `openAiBody` in `engine/src/model.ts` checks `request.provider === 'openrouter'` for usage accounting (`stream_options.include_usage` + `usage: { include: true }`). Added `phorma-cloud` to those checks so the proxy gets usage/cost data for metering. The `phorma-cloud` adapter in `ADAPTERS` reuses `openAiCompatible('https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions', false)` — `requiresKey: false` because the local client never holds a key (the proxy does).
- 2026-07-12 — `PhormaCloudService.sessionToken()` is the public method to resolve a fresh Clerk JWT for the proxy (added 2026-07-12). Don't access `clerk.session$` from outside the service — it's private. The method returns `null` when signed out.
- 2026-07-12 — BYO live model fetch: `ModelTransportService.listModels(provider)` mirrors `listBedrockModels` — desktop → Rust `list_provider_models` cmd; browser → direct fetch (CORS best-effort, falls back to free text). Rust `list_provider_models` in `llm.rs` supports anthropic/openai/gemini/openrouter. Gemini uses `?key=` query param; Anthropic uses `x-api-key` + `anthropic-version` header; OpenAI/OpenRouter use Bearer. Registered in `lib.rs` `generate_handler!`.
- 2026-07-12 — UI gating: Phorma Cloud provider only appears in the picker when `phormaCloud.subscribed()` is true. In both `prompt-panel.ts` and `settings-dialog.ts`, `providers` changed from a plain array to a `computed()` signal that filters `MODEL_PROVIDERS`. GOTCHA: templates MUST call it as `providers()` not `providers` — `ng build` catches this (TS2322: `Signal<...[]>>` not assignable to `any[]`). Phorma Cloud is excluded from `keyedProviders` in settings (no API key needed).
- 2026-08-25 - Every `ModelRequest` built OUTSIDE the run engine must spread `settings.providerEndpoints()` (`ollamaBaseUrl`, `lmstudioBaseUrl`, `bedrockRegion`). `RunControllerService` and `EvalRunnerService` passed all three; the four `ModelRequest` literals in `WorkflowBuilderService` (Ask, Plan turn, Plan palette, Agent loop) and the two in `FieldGenerationService` passed NONE, so the engine silently fell back to `us-east-1` / `localhost`. Symptom: an assistant chat on a Bedrock default model died with `bedrock request failed (400 Bad Request): "The provided model identifier is invalid."` while the identical model ran fine from the canvas - a geographic inference profile (`au.`/`eu.`/`apac.`/`us.`) only resolves in a region inside its own geography, and the URL region is what the adapter builds from `bedrockRegion`. A remote Ollama or LM Studio server was unreachable from the assistant for the same reason.
- 2026-08-25 - Claude Opus 4.7 onward REJECT sampling params: sending `temperature` (or `top_p`/`top_k`) to Sonnet 5, Opus 4.7/4.8/5 or Fable 5 is a hard 400 (`` `temperature` is deprecated for this model ``), and there is no accepted value - the field must be absent. `acceptsSamplingParams(model)` in `engine/src/model.ts` gates all three wire builders (`converseBody`, `anthropicBody`, `openAiBody`) through `wireTemperature`, which returns `undefined` so `JSON.stringify` drops the key. Matched on the MODEL ID, not the provider: the same model arrives as `claude-sonnet-5`, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`, `au.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5` and `anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-20260115-v1:0`. The pattern deliberately does not match `claude-sonnet-4-5`, which rejects only `temperature` AND `top_p` together (the engine never sends `top_p`). Covered by `engine/src/model-sampling.spec.ts`.
- 2026-08-25 - `ModelTransportService.testModel({provider, model})` is the reachability probe behind Settings > Models > Test. It goes through `create()` on purpose, so it exercises the real key resolution, proxy, region and wire format; a probe with its own HTTP path can pass while inference still fails. It sends no `temperature`. Listing a model catalog is NOT a substitute - `list_bedrock_models` / `list_bedrock_inference_profiles` answer per region and say nothing about whether an id is invocable from the configured one. On a Bedrock `ValidationException` the dialog appends the geo-prefix-vs-region hint, which is the actual cause almost every time.

## Usage Credits (abstraction over real USD inference cost)

- 2026-07-12 — Phorma Cloud NEVER shows dollars to the user. `TierLimits` now has `monthlyCredits` (round marketing number, the ONLY billing unit displayed) alongside `monthlyCostUsd` (real spend cap → OpenRouter key limit, analytics-only). Tiers in `cloud/src/tenants.ts` TIERS (plus tier REMOVED 2026-07-19): starter {1000cr,$4}, pro {3000cr,$12.60}, team {10000cr,$44}. Base burn = 125 credits/$1 at the ORIGINAL (pre-margin-fix) ratio; higher tiers include a volume bonus (pro +5%, team +10%) baked into a LARGER USD budget so a credit buys more real inference — credit numbers stay round regardless of the USD side. Prices (margin ref, not yet enforced): $20/$60/$200 → 80%/79%/78% margin.
- 2026-07-12 — MARGIN FIX: initial pass used `monthlyCostUsd` ≈ 40% of price (60/58/56% margin). Cloudflare infra cost was confirmed negligible (~$0.00003/run across DO duration+requests, D1 row writes, KV cache-bust delete — the $5/mo Workers Paid base is shared across all tenants) so it's NOT a margin lever. Dropped the ratio to ~20% of price to hit a 75-80% target — this ONLY changes `monthlyCostUsd` per tier (halved: 8→4, 16.32→8.16, 25.2→12.6, 88→44). `monthlyCredits` and every display/API/frontend surface is UNTOUCHED — that's the entire point of the credits abstraction: the real budget can move without any user-visible change.
- 2026-07-12 — `creditsForTier(tier, costUsd)` + `creditsPerUsd(tier)` in `tenants.ts` are the ONLY dollars→credits conversion. `GET /api/me` returns `creditsUsed`/`creditsLimit` (+ costUsd* kept for analytics). Frontend `PhormaCloudProfile.quota` mirrors both; `PhormaCloudService.creditsFraction` (renamed from `costFraction`) + `creditsPerUsd` computed (derives burn rate from quota, falls back to 125). Cloud dialog chip + Settings quota panel show credits via `| number` (DecimalPipe). Quota-exhausted error strings say "Monthly credits exhausted".
- 2026-07-12 — Runs panel shows per-run cost in credits ONLY for Phorma Cloud runs, keeps $ for BYO. Mechanism: engine `node-usage` event gained a `provider: string` field (`engine/src/events.ts` + emit in `engine.ts` — `provider` already in scope at the emit site). `RunControllerService.runUsage` gained a `phormaCloud: boolean` flag (OR'd true when any node-usage has `provider === 'phorma-cloud'`). Runs-panel `usageCredits` computed converts costUsd via `phormaCloud.creditsPerUsd()`. Cloud DO consumer of node-usage (`workflow-agent.ts`) only reads `event.usage`, so the new field flows through the relay untouched.
- 2026-07-12 — GOTCHA: `npx tsc` in `engine/` and `cloud/` tries to install the WRONG package `tsc@2.0.4` (neither has a local typescript). Use the frontend's binary instead: `./frontend/node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit -p engine/tsconfig.json` (and `-p cloud/tsconfig.json`). Frontend build is `cd frontend && npx ng build`.
- 2026-07-12 — GOTCHA: swapping a template pipe (e.g. `currency` → `number`) requires updating the standalone component's `imports:` array too — remove `CurrencyPipe`, add `DecimalPipe` from `@angular/common`. `ng build` fails with "No pipe found with name 'number'" pointing at the template line. Runs-panel keeps BOTH (BYO still shows $).
- 2026-07-12 — Model picker UX: Phorma Cloud uses a non-editable `p-select` (`[editable]="false"`) from the curated `PROVIDER_MODEL_SUGGESTIONS['phorma-cloud']`. BYO providers use an editable `p-select` (`[editable]="true"`) populated by `listModels`, with free-text fallback on fetch error (mirrors the Bedrock pattern). The `showModelDropdown` computed gates dropdown-vs-text-input per provider.
- 2026-07-12 — Pre-existing build errors unrelated to this feature: `@tauri-apps/plugin-updater` and `@tauri-apps/plugin-process` modules not found in `update.service.ts` (present before these changes). Don't confuse them with feature errors.
- 2026-07-12 — UX refinement: Phorma Cloud is a SELECTABLE provider option whenever signed in (no `(subscribe)` suffix, not disabled). When selected WITHOUT an active subscription, both the node model picker (`prompt-panel`) and Settings default-model picker HIDE the model selector and show a "Subscribe to Phorma Cloud" CTA block instead (`needsPhormaCloudSubscription` computed = provider is phorma-cloud AND `!subscribed()`). The Subscribe button deep-links to Settings → Cloud (`SettingsDialogService.open('cloud')` / `dialog.activePageId.set('cloud')`).
- 2026-07-12 — Buy Credits (top-up) placeholder: `CREDIT_PACKS` in `frontend/src/app/core/credit-packs.ts` — Small $9.99/400cr (84%), Medium $19.99/900cr (82%), Large $39.99/2000cr (80%, deliberately EXACTLY the $0.02/credit subscription rate so top-ups can tie but never beat subscribing — keeps upgrading the rational choice for sustained heavy use). `CreditsDialogService` + `CreditsDialog` (`workspace/cloud/credits-dialog*`) mirror `CloudDialogService`/`CloudDialog` exactly (overlay/card SCSS pattern); all 3 pack buttons are disabled "Coming soon" — no payment backend yet. Registered in `app.ts`/`app.html` next to `CloudDialog`. Two entry points: (1) Settings → Cloud → Phorma quota panel, a "Buy more credits" button right after the credits bar; (2) `RunControllerService`'s `run-failed` handler matches `event.error` against `/credits exhausted/i` and fires a `toast.error(...)` with a "Buy credits" action button — the 402 message from `resolveHostedInference` flows unaltered through engine `node-failed`→`run-failed`, no wrapping needed. GOTCHA: only the credits-exhausted case gets a toast; other run failures keep the pre-existing console/trace-only behavior (don't add a generic toast for all failures — that was scope creep, reverted).
- 2026-07-12 — `ToastService`/`Toast` (`shared/toast/`) gained an optional `action?: {label, onClick}` on `ToastOptions` + the `warning()`/`error()` helpers (3rd param). Renders a `.phorma-toast__cta` button in the toast body; clicking it dismisses the toast THEN calls `onClick`. Use this pattern for any future "toast with a CTA" needs instead of inventing a new mechanism.
- 2026-07-12 — **STRIPE NOT WIRED UP YET (TODO/future).** The "Subscribe" CTA is a PLACEHOLDER — it only deep-links to the Cloud settings page. There is no Stripe checkout, no payment flow, and no way for a user to actually activate a subscription from the app yet. Tenant provisioning is still manual via admin-token-gated `POST /api/provision`. When Stripe lands: wire the Subscribe button to a Stripe Checkout session, and a Stripe webhook worker should call the existing `/api/provision` + `/api/deactivate` endpoints (they were designed for this — no schema change needed). Until then, `subscribed()` only flips true after manual provisioning against a hosted-mode worker.
- 2026-07-12 — `anyComponentStyle` budget raised 12kB→14kB warning / 16kB→18kB error (`angular.json`) — settings-dialog.scss legitimately grew with the Phorma Cloud subscribe CTA block. Consolidate duplicated rules before raising further.

## Robustness Primitives (EPIC 3, shipped 2026-07-19)

- 2026-07-19 — Retry/fallback/timeout/compression all live INSIDE one `executeNode` call (`runAgent`'s `streamRoundRobustly`), so the journal key (minted once per executeNode) stays stable — internal retries are replay-safe. Never move retries above executeNode.
- 2026-07-19 — Error classification: `ModelRequestError` (engine/src/model.ts) carries `status`; `isTransientModelError` treats 408/429/5xx/network as retryable, other 4xx as permanent. The Tauri Rust proxy throws plain strings — the classifier falls back to parsing `(\d{3})` out of the message, so keep the `"{provider} request failed ({status}): …"` message format stable in all clients.
- 2026-07-19 — `RunGate.sleep(ms)` is the interruptible backoff/wait primitive: it registers a waiter so `stop()` wakes it immediately (throws RunStoppedError). Never use bare setTimeout for delays inside the engine.
- 2026-07-19 — Workflow timeout: local = pause-aware clock in `WorkflowRun` (banks running ms on pause via gate.onPauseChange, re-arms timer on resume, `unref()` the timer); timeout sets `timedOut` then `gate.stop()`, and `execute()` maps the resulting RunStoppedError to `run-failed` ("Workflow timed out…"). Cloud = engine deadline (remaining budget after resume) + `this.schedule(…, 'workflowTimedOut', runId)` durable alarm whose ONLY job is waking an evicted DO; cancel alarms with callback === 'workflowTimedOut' at settle.
- 2026-07-19 — Error branch: `AgentNodeData.errorPortId` stores the port base id explicitly (NOT positional — agents have user-visible ports). `errorRoutePortId()` requires the port to exist AND have a connected handoff, else fail-fast. On success the agent restricts `viaPortIds` to non-error out-ports so success never leaks through "On error". The catch that routes errors wraps ONLY `runNodeBody` — downstream failures must not be captured by an ancestor's branch.
- 2026-07-19 — Error Handler node (`error-handler` kind): run `execute()` catch invokes it best-effort with a JSON `{error, at}` payload before emitting `run-failed`; a stopped gate is swapped for a fresh RunGate during handler execution (restore after). Handler failures never mask the original error; run still settles failed (heym semantics).
- 2026-07-19 — Context compression: `pricing.ts` `ModelPrice.contextTokens` synced from OpenRouter `context_length` (localStorage cache key bumped to `phorma.model-price-table.v2` — bump it whenever the row shape changes); engine gets `RunOptions.contextWindow` lookup fn. Compression keeps first user message + last 2 tool rounds, summary rides as a USER message (Anthropic rejects back-to-back assistant turns). Summarizer failure returns messages untouched — never fails the node.
- 2026-07-19 — GOTCHA: `Record<ModelProviderId, …>` maps in cloud/ (PROVIDER_ENV_KEYS, OPENROUTER_SLUG_PREFIX) break silently/loudly when a provider is added to the union — lmstudio was missing from BOTH (one tsc error, one silent undefined-prefix bug). When adding a ModelProviderId, grep cloud/src for existing Record maps.
- 2026-07-19 — Playwright vs canvas: click-to-add palette buttons drop nodes at the canvas centre (they can stack); node drags need a real movement threshold (small first move, then the real drag). Port-to-port wiring works by mouse.down on the port dot → move → up on the target port circle, but coordinates come from screenshots — re-screenshot after every layout change. PREFER `window.__phormaTest` (below) over any of this.

## Test Suite Quality (audit 2026-08-14)

- 2026-08-14 - THERE IS NOW CI: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs engine vitest + `tsc` + the 11 scenario scripts, cloud `test:unit` + `check`, frontend karma + production build, and `cargo check --locked` on every push and PR. Before it, `release.yml` was the only workflow (tag-triggered, build-only) and ~1700 assertions ran only when a human remembered. If you add a suite, add it to `ci.yml` in the same change or it does not exist.

A scenario script that crashes before its first assertion still prints nothing alarming. This is why the runner treats a non-zero exit as failure and why CI runs it.

- 2026-08-14 - Mutation testing is the only honest way to grade a test. Procedure that worked: read the file with `[IO.File]::ReadAllText($absolutePath)` (it resolves against the PROCESS cwd, not the shell's - use an absolute path), `.Replace()` one realistic bug, run the targeted suite, restore the exact original text. Do NOT `git checkout` to revert while in-flight feature work is uncommitted.

- 2026-08-15 - Writing an "accepts exactly X" property against a regex-based validator: restate the shape as structural predicates (split the value at its separator, check each part's alphabet) instead of importing the production pattern. For `cloud-aws/src/core/config.ts`'s `IMAGE_URI_RE` the split is unambiguous because neither the tag nor the digest alphabet contains `@`, `:` or `/` - first `@` else last `:`. The independent oracle then makes both halves mutation-sensitive: relaxing the registry class to `[A-Za-z0-9.-]` fails on `DOCKER.IO/phorma:a`, and flipping `triggerApiUrl`'s trailing-slash flag fails on `https://.../`.
- 2026-08-15 - The WHATWG URL parser rewrites scheme-relative forms for its six special schemes, so `new URL('https:/host')` yields `https://host/` and `new URL('HTTPS://host').protocol` is `https:`. Any oracle that restates an endpoint shape by string prefix must therefore lower-case the scheme comparison and keep `:`-bearing junk out of its free-form generator, or it will disagree with a `new URL`-based validator on inputs nobody documented. `config.ts` also checks `?`, `#` and surrounding whitespace against the SUPPLIED string because the parser normalizes all three away.
- 2026-08-14 - Engine `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` covers `src/**` only, and `*.spec.ts` type errors sat in it unnoticed (a `WorkflowNode` literal missing `category`/`icon`/`position`, `WorkflowPort` literals using `type`/`label` instead of `name`/`role`). CI runs this step now. `test/**/*.mts` is still NOT type-checked - it needs `@types/node` for `process`, and 16 `startRun` calls omit the required `requestInput`.
- 2026-08-16 - "The URL equals what the registry says" is not a test that the registry produced it: a literal in the service that agrees with the registry today passes. The half that bites is patching the registry entry (`DEPLOY_TARGETS[target].instanceUrl` and `endpoints[op].path` are plain mutable properties) to emit a sentinel, then asserting the emitted URL carries it and that no fragment the registry owns survives. Restore in a `finally` - `phorma` and `cloudflare` SHARE one endpoint table, so patching through one target patches the other. Parenthesize the sentinel (`/@registry-path(status)`), or the op name re-forms `/status` and the fragment scan false-fails. Check fragments only AFTER the base: `https://trigger.example.test` contains `/trigger` inside the scheme's `//`.
- 2026-08-16 - `get_diagnostics` on a frontend spec came back clean on a `TS2352` (`CloudEndpointContext` cast to `Record<string, string>`) that `ng test`'s bundler then failed on. Treat a clean diagnostics read as necessary, never sufficient - run the suite.
- 2026-08-16 - PowerShell's `>` redirect writes UTF-16LE, so a karma log captured that way matches nothing when read as utf8. Read it back with `readFileSync(path, 'utf16le')` and strip the ANSI colour codes (`/\u001b\[[0-9;]*m/g`) before grepping for `FAILED`. Piping karma through `Select-String` in the same command line also truncates and reorders in this shell - redirect, then parse in Node.
